canada.ca — Line 22200 (deduction for CPP contributions on self-employment income) and Line 31000 (base CPP credit) · current (2025 page; same structure for 2026) · the employer half plus the enhanced part are deducted from income; the base part is a credit (used in the $5,155 and $4,227 calculations)

CRA T4127 Payroll Deductions Formulas, 122nd ed. (Jan 2026), as recorded in salary/PRODUCTION-BIBLE.md · 2026 · federal 14% to $58,523, BPA $16,452 → federal tax $5,155.43; Manitoba 10.8% to $47,000, 12.75% to $100,000, BPA $15,780 → Manitoba tax $4,226.55
canada.ca — Who has to pay: required tax instalments for individuals · 2026 · instalments are required for 2026 if net tax owing is over $3,000 in 2026 and in 2025 or 2024 ($1,800 in Québec)

Example assumptions (on-screen footer): 2026 · Manitoba · single · $60K NET self-employment income · no other income or deductions. A different province, income, RRSP contributions or other income changes every number. General info, not advice. yt.description:
Self-employed in Canada? Nobody withholds tax for you, so here's the real math on a $1,000 invoice.

Example (2026, Manitoba, single, $60,000 net self-employment income, no other income or deductions):
CPP (both halves, 11.9%): $6,724
Federal tax: $5,155
Manitoba tax: $4,227
Total: about $16,106, roughly 27% of net income.

But that's the average. In this example, each extra dollar costs about 36¢. A simple habit: move about $270 of every $1,000 into a separate tax account the day you're paid. And if your net tax owing is over $3,000 this year and in one of the last two, you may have to pay by instalments.

Different province or income = different numbers. Sources: CRA (canada.ca, line 22200; required tax instalments), CRA T4127 2026. General information, not tax advice.

_vo: You send a client a thousand-dollar invoice. How much of it is actually yours? Self-employed? Nobody takes tax off for you. Say you net sixty thousand dollars this year, in Manitoba. First, C-P-P. You pay both halves. About six thousand, seven hundred. Federal tax: about five thousand, one hundred and fifty. Manitoba: about four thousand, two hundred. Add it up: about sixteen thousand, one hundred dollars. Roughly twenty-seven percent. But that's an average. In this example, each extra dollar costs about thirty-six cents. So from every thousand-dollar invoice, move about two hundred and seventy dollars into a separate tax account. The day it's paid. Owe more than three thousand, this year and in one of the last two? You may have to pay in instalments. The invoice isn't your income. What's left after tax is.
